- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cubism is a pivotal movement that revolutionized the art world, primarily led by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key artists associated with Cubism include Pablo Picasso, Georges Braque, Juan Gris, Albert Gleizes, and Fernand Léger.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pablo Picasso's notable works include "Les Demoiselles d'Avignon" (1907) and "Guernica" (1937).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Georges Braque's notable works include "Violin and Pitcher" (1910) and "The Portuguese" (1911).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Juan Gris's notable works include "The Breakfast Table" (1914) and "The Painter's Family" (1923).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Albert Gleizes's notable works include "Les Joueurs de Football" (1912-1913) and "Les Baigneuses" (1912-1913).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Fernand Léger's notable works include "Contrast of Forms" (1913) and "The City" (1919).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Characteristics of Cubist art include fragmentation, multiple viewpoints, overlapping planes, abstracted forms, and monochromatic color schemes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cubism influenced a wide range of avant-garde movements, including Futurism, Constructivism, and Surrealism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Frida Kahlo's artistic style is characterized by vibrant colors, symbolism and imagery, self-portraiture, naïve folk art influence, and surrealist elements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Frida Kahlo's inspirations include Mexican culture and folk art, personal experience and suffering, Diego Rivera and the Mexican Muralist Movement, surrealism and European modernism, and mythology and folklore.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some of Frida Kahlo's most famous works include "The Two Fridas" (1939), "Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird" (1940), and "The Broken Column" (1944).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Frida Kahlo's relationship with Diego Rivera began in 1927 when they met, and they married in 1929.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Frida and Diego's marriage was marked by intense passion, mutual admiration, and infidelity.
